recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source edit is needed unless FHIR-I changes the transaction-only semantics or moves extension ownership again; otherwise edits would duplicate or risk drifting from the maintained Extension Pack definition.
issue_request: FHIR-34343 was a Published FHIR-I R5 change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked how clients can request version-specific references to resources whose ids or versions are assigned during transaction processing without using invalid versioned urn:uuid or urn:oid temporary references. The resolution chose a boolean resolve-as-version-specific extension, limited to references in a transaction that target resources being created or updated in the same transaction, with graceful fallback when unsupported.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in d5f982f6433fbb9bf79cf55ad9d6181f99e7d643, which added HTTP transaction guidance and updated the then-current Reference extension source. The extension definition has since moved out of core into the FHIR Extension Pack, while core keeps links to that maintained definition.
additional_context: FHIR-34344 clarified how existing version-specific references behave in transactions; FHIR-38648 fixed the broken link and duplicate narrative from the original text; FHIR-38649 broadened the extension context to uri and url in the Extension Pack; and FHIR-43600 added a Provenance-oriented transaction example. Those related issues already have reconcile commits on the combined branch, so they were not republished here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. source/http.html already links to resolve-as-version-specific, states the transaction-only semantics, describes unsupported fallback to a version-agnostic reference, and requires supporting systems to remove the extension during transaction reference resolution. The Extension Pack StructureDefinition defines the active extension with the expected canonical URL, boolean value, cardinality, context, and transaction-only comment, and source/bundle/bundle-transaction.xml demonstrates the extension on Provenance.target references.
